description: Producer Herta Studio; consumer server-only ivrm-web. POST /api/ivrm/community-game-stats/read. Key=HMAC-SHA256(IVRM_INTEGRATION_TOKEN,herta-community-game-stats-read-v1); signature=HMAC-SHA256(key,timestamp.eventId.POST.path.rawBody). Headers X-IVRM-Timestamp ISO, X-IVRM-Event-Id UUID, X-IVRM-Signature hex. Five-minute freshness, no query, max8192bytes. Signing is unchanged from v1 (the v1 purpose string remains the key-derivation domain separator); the contract version is negotiated by the signed request field version: absent or 1 returns exactly the v1 response (overviewResponse / userResponse), 2 returns the same game sections plus a required activity section (overviewResponseV2 / userResponseV2), 3 adds the insights sections and the game mode (overviewResponseV3 / userResponseV3 / gameResponse), and 4 adds the overview channels section and messageCharUnits on the user activity (overviewResponseV4 / userResponseV4); the game mode accepts version 3 or 4 with an unchanged shape, and 5 returns the unified game identity view (overviewResponseV5 / userResponseV5 / gameResponseV5) in which games are unified across localized and client-specific activity names, and 6 adds the overview leaderboards section (overviewResponseV6), and 7 adds the overview weeklyChampions section (overviewResponseV7) and the channel mode (channelResponse), the user and game responses unchanged from v5. The source of truth stays Herta community_game_activity_daily for games and community_activity_daily for activity; ivrm-web relays each read and stores no copy (ivrm-web #1703 S1/S4b, Herta #998). Request range from/to is a JST local_date range. mode is optional and defaults to overview: overview returns meta.earliestDate (the guild-wide first observed date, not range-limited), the top 25 games by totalSeconds with playerCount, and the user ranking paginated by limit/offset (max 100, ordered by totalSeconds desc then discordUserId asc; each entry carries its topGameName). mode=user requires discordUserId (and overview forbids it) and returns that user's totalSeconds plus their top 25 games. The v2 activity section is built only from the community_activity_daily metrics voice_seconds, messages and online_seconds (reactions are excluded: accumulated too sparsely). messages counts only the messages the bot's Activity Rules counted (cooldown-filtered), never the guild's raw message total; voice_seconds is stay time in countable voice channels; online_seconds is presence time and is a reference total only. overview activity carries guild totals for the range (voiceSeconds, messageCount, onlineSeconds, plus voiceMemberCount / messageMemberCount distinct-user counts) and the voice and message rankings, paginated by the same limit/offset as the game ranking (ordered by value desc then discordUserId asc). user activity carries only that user's voiceSeconds, messageCount and onlineSeconds for the range. Activity is fail-soft per section: when the activity read fails, activity is null while the game sections still return ok. All members are returned; opt-out filtering is applied by the ivrm-web relay, not here. Items carry aggregated seconds/counts only: no Rich Presence details/state, no message content, no raw session rows. All responses private,no-store. Version 3 returns the v2 sections plus a required insights section on overview and user, and unlocks mode=game (version 3 only). Overview insights carry the period totals (totalSeconds and distinct playerCount), a member-by-game matrix over the period's top 15 games (games ordered by totalSeconds desc then name asc; members ordered by their period total desc then discordUserId asc; secondsByGame aligns with games and zero-fills games a member did not play), the weekday distribution of play seconds as a Monday-first array of 7, and momentum for the same top 15 games (recentSeconds inside the trailing 7 days of the range, and newPlayerCount of players whose first observed play of that game falls inside the range). User insights carry playDays inside the range, longestStreakDays and currentStreakDays computed over the whole observed history up to the range end (streaks are personal-panel data only and are never ranked), lastPlayDate, the daily series inside the range (days without play are omitted), and the user's Monday-first weekday distribution. mode=game requires gameName and returns that game's totals with first/last observed play dates inside the range, every player's seconds paginated by limit/offset (ordered by totalSeconds desc then discordUserId asc), and viewer (null unless discordUserId is given): the viewer's competition rank over all players (null when the viewer has no play of the game in the range) and totalSeconds; the relay recomputes the viewer rank after opt-out filtering. Insights are fail-soft per section like activity: when an insights read fails, insights is null while the other sections still return ok; the game mode is a main content and fails with 503 instead. A game with no play inside the range returns zeroed game totals with null dates and an empty players list. Version 4 (ivrm-web #2035 S6, Herta #1054): the overview gains a required channels section, fail-soft like activity and insights (null when its read fails, while the other sections still return ok). channels.recordedFrom is the guild-wide first date of community_activity_channel_daily (not range-limited, null when the table holds no row for the guild); channel recording starts later than the activity totals, so the channel sums deliberately do not add up to the activity totals and consumers must say so. channels.voiceChannels and channels.messageChannels are the top 25 channels of the range by voice_seconds / messages from community_activity_channel_daily, each with memberCount (distinct users with a row in that channel). Channel names are not stored in the database: name is resolved by Studio from the bot guild options and is null when the channel no longer resolves (deleted, or the bot unreachable); a name is never invented, and consumers fall back to an id-derived label. channels.charUnits carries the message_char_units totals and the member ranking paginated like the other rankings. message_char_units is the bot's character-points metric: one unit per half-width (ASCII) character and two units per full-width character, excluding URLs, custom emoji, Unicode emoji and whitespace; points are units / 2, and the wire carries raw integer units only. The v4 user activity (activityUserV4) adds the user's own messageCharUnits to the three v2 fields; the v2/v3 activity shapes are unchanged. Version 5 game identity (Herta #1060 S7b): since S7a the daily rows also record the Discord application_id (empty when the presence carried none, which covers all rows before S7a). A row belongs to a canonical game when its application_id is listed in the guild's Activity Rules gameIdentityMappings, else it groups by application_id, else — for id-less rows — by a mapped activity name (aliases and the canonical name itself), else by its recorded name. A game's key is app:<applicationId> (for a mapped game, the mapping's first id) or name:<activityName>; name is the display name: the canonical name when mapped, else the name the group accumulated the most seconds under in the range. applicationId is null for name groups. The overview ranking items add topGameKey next to topGameName (now the unified display name). The game mode at version 5 accepts exactly one selector: gameName (the exact recorded name, figures identical to v3/v4; key/applicationId report the unified identity that name resolves to), gameApplicationId, or gameKey (app:<id> or name:<name>), the latter two returning the whole unified game's figures; a unified game with no rows in range reports zeroed figures, with name falling back to the canonical name, the name key's name, or the key itself for an unknown application id. The activity, channels, insights-user and weekday/totals payloads are unchanged from v4. Mappings are applied at read time on the supply side only; stored rows are never rewritten, and unmapped games keep their recorded name as their key. Version 6 leaderboards (ivrm-web #2111 S9, Herta #1081): the overview gains a required leaderboards section, fail-soft like activity and insights (null when its read fails, while the other sections still return ok). leaderboards.gameCount ranks members by the number of distinct unified games (the v5 identity) they played in the range; because application_id recording only started on 2026-11-28, earlier rows unify by name only, so counts over ranges reaching back mix name-based and id-based unification. leaderboards.playDays ranks members by the number of distinct activity dates with play in the range (the user insights playDays figure, ranked). leaderboards.growth ranks members by the absolute increase of total play seconds against the previous period — the window of the same length immediately before the range — and carries previousRange {from, to} naming that window; only members whose previous-period total is at least 3600 seconds and whose increase is positive are listed, so a range whose previous period precedes observation (such as the cumulative range starting at the first observed date) yields an empty growth ranking. All three rankings paginate by the same limit/offset as the game ranking, ordered by value descending then discordUserId ascending. Streaks remain personal-panel data and are never ranked; online seconds and reactions stay excluded from the rankings. Version 7 (ivrm-web #2115 S10, Herta #1082): the overview gains a required weeklyChampions section, fail-soft like activity and insights (null when its read fails, while the other sections still return ok). weeklyChampions.weeks lists, for every Monday-start week the range touches, that week's leader candidates by total play seconds (ordered by totalSeconds desc then discordUserId asc), capped at 5 per week: weekStart is the week's Monday and weekEnd its Sunday (JST calendar dates; the first and last weeks may extend beyond the range, and candidates are ranked over the days inside the range only). The section deliberately carries no title counts and no fixed champion: the relay counts weekly titles from this raw list, promoting the next candidate when a week's leader is opted out, so the supply never applies opt-out here. Weeks with no play inside the range are omitted. Version 7 also unlocks mode=channel (version 7 only), following the game mode's selector pattern: the request names channelId and channelMetric (voice or messages) and returns that channel's member ranking from community_activity_channel_daily, paginated by the same limit/offset as the other rankings (ordered by value desc then discordUserId asc). The response carries the channel's total and distinct memberCount for the range (the same figures the v4 channels section aggregates for that channel), recordedFrom (the guild-wide first date of community_activity_channel_daily, not range-limited; channel sums deliberately do not add up to the activity totals, as with the v4 channels section), the channel name resolved by Studio from the bot guild options (null when the channel no longer resolves, as in v4), and viewer (null unless discordUserId is given): the viewer's competition rank over all members of the channel (null when the viewer has no record in it) and their value; the relay recomputes the viewer rank after opt-out filtering. Items and the viewer carry totalSeconds for voice and totalCount for messages, matching channel.metric. Like the game mode, the channel mode is a main content and fails with 503 instead of degrading; a channel with no rows in the range returns zeroed totals and an empty ranking.
